benefit.name: Medical Equipment & Devices Supplement
benefit.amount: Full cost of pre-approved equipment — e.g., scooters up to $3,500 ($4,500 bariatric), floor/ceiling lifts up to $4,200 (more only if the excess is from unusual installation expenses); wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds and bathing aids at ministry rates
benefit.summary: The ministry buys, repairs and replaces essential medical equipment — canes to power wheelchairs, hospital beds, transfer aids, pressure-relief mattresses, specialized glucose meters — for people on assistance with no other way to pay.
benefit.note: Pre-approval is required: the ministry must approve the request before purchase, except in cases of a life-threatening emergency, and it is the payer of last resort — other available resources (for example ICBC, WorkSafeBC or private insurance) must be considered first. Co-funding may be considered when other resources cannot pay the entire cost.

detail.about: Covered items include canes, crutches, walkers, manual and power wheelchairs, scooters, grab bars, bath seats, commodes, lift devices, hospital beds, pressure-relief mattresses and non-conventional glucose meters. The item must be prescribed by a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner, and/or the medical need confirmed by the assessment of a relevant therapist (occupational or physical therapist). Many items also need a therapist assessment. Most equipment can be replaced every five years (wheelchair seating after two; canes, crutches and walkers as needed). Scooters intended primarily for recreational or sports use, lift chairs, automatic turning beds and containment type beds are not provided.

steps: Contact the ministry through My Self Serve or 1-866-866-0800 to start an equipment request
Get a prescription from your doctor or nurse practitioner, and/or an assessment from a relevant therapist confirming the medical need
Complete an occupational or physical therapist assessment where required (wheelchairs, seating, scooters, lifts)
Submit supplier quote(s); wait for written ministry pre-approval
The ministry pays the supplier directly; repairs are requested the same way
documents: Doctor or nurse practitioner prescription and/or therapist assessment confirming the medical need
Occupational/physical therapist assessment for mobility and positioning items
tips: Never buy first — the ministry will not accept payment responsibility for equipment purchased without prior approval, except in cases of a life-threatening emergency
If you need specific features, ask your OT to note why the least-expensive option would not meet your medical need.
Repairs and batteries can be covered between replacement cycles
detail.time: Weeks to a couple of months depending on assessments, quotes and pre-approval

values.note: pre-approved medical equipment at ministry rates
